subject: PrivDeploy IaC: Drain + Circuit-Breaker Matrix and Rollout Orchestration
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Singh <ravi.singh@blueharbor.com>; Elaine Park <elaine.park@blueharbor.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivDeploy IaC: Drain + Circuit-Breaker Matrix and Rollout Orchestration

Hi Ravi / Elaine —

Thanks again for the architecture walkthrough last week. As we get closer to the pilot for BlueHarbor’s VPC/on-prem private deployment, we want to align on the operational controls we’ll bake into the IaC and CI pipeline so the rollout is deterministic and safe.

Attached: priv-iac-drain-cb-matrix.xlsx (proposed matrix), playbook-draft.md, and a small tf-module compatibility patch for review. High-level asks from our side: 

- Confirm desired circuit-breaker semantics (per-cluster vs per-tenant) and default thresholds (error %, request timeout).
- Agree drain strategy for node replacement and canary traffic (graceful drain window, health-check backoff).
- Decide which Terraform/Helm/Ansible artifacts are the canonical sources of truth for: networking (VPC routing/NAT), firewall rules, and bastion/egress policies.
- CI gating: smoke + traffic-sim tests we run in staging before merge + rollback windows.

Notes on the matrix (see attached): we propose a conservative default to start — CB tripped at 5% 5min window for customer-critical routes; graceful drain = 120s with delayed termination hook; canary ramp 5/25/50/100 over 30m. We can loosen thresholds after one successful pilot run.

Neha/Karthik: I’m looping you in for technical validation and to call out any upstream module changes required. Lauren: can you coordinate the operational playbook with BlueHarbor SRE and confirm ownership on the runbook steps?

Ravi / Elaine — could you review the attached matrix and highlight any hard constraints from your end (security, procurement timelines, or in-house runbook requirements)? If we’re aligned, propose a working session Tues or Wed to lock the final matrix and CI gating checklist.

Thanks —
Marissa
SVP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: priv-iac-drain-cb-matrix.xlsx (worksheet), playbook-draft.md (markdown), tf-module-compatibility.patch (text)

Subject: Re: PrivDeploy IaC: Drain + Circuit-Breaker Matrix and Rollout Orchestration

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. I skimmed the matrix; it looks sensible. A couple of immediate points from BlueHarbor SRE: 

- Our security policy requires that CB decisions are auditable and logged to an internal SIEM (we can provide the ingestion endpoint). Will your runtime emit the CB events we need?
- For node drain: we require a configurable pre-drain hook to trigger a host-level compliance scatter (our patch manager runs before termination). Can that be surfaced as an Ansible hook?
- Terraform: we need a compatibility guarantee for current networking TF modules — any breaking changes must be flagged in the PR with a migration plan.

Procurement: we are tracking the pilot timeline; we’re targeting an initial staging rollout in the week of June 14. Any gating that pushes the deadline will need a follow-up with procurement (cc’d).

I’m available Tue 10–12 PT or Wed 13–15 PT for a working session.

—Ravi
Head of Platform Engineering
BlueHarbor Systems

Subject: Re: PrivDeploy IaC: Drain + Circuit-Breaker Matrix and Rollout Orchestration

Thanks — quick technical response + proposed defaults so BlueHarbor can validate. I’ve attached a small tf patch and a playbook excerpt that demonstrate the hook points.

Key points:

1) Circuit-breaker telemetry and logging
- Runtime will emit CB state transitions (armed/triggered/cleared) to stdout and send structured events to our observability endpoint. We can wire an extra exporter to push a copy to BlueHarbor’s SIEM (we’ll need the intake URL + auth token).

2) Drain strategy and Ansible hooks
- We support a pre-drain and post-drain Ansible hook. The pre-drain hook payload includes instance metadata (id, ip, tenant). Recommend pre-drain hook = run compliance scatter; post-drain = re-register metrics consumer.
- Default graceful drain window = 120s; if BlueHarbor needs 300s we can template that in the Helm values (values.global.drainGraceSec).

3) Terraform/Helm module boundaries
- Proposal: Terraform for cloud/VPC-level networking and static routing, Helm for service-level config and health-check parameters, Ansible for ad-hoc host-level operations.
- Backwards-compatibility: we’ll tag a compatibility matrix in the TF module PRs. The patch attached shows a non-breaking rename that keeps old variables as deprecated aliases (see tf-module-compatibility.patch). CI will fail if module API changes without a migration note.

4) CI gating and traffic-sim tests
- Staging pipeline will run a traffic-sim job that validates success rate > 99.5% under a synthetic 5% error injection for 60s. Canary ramp will be: 5% for 10m, 25% for 20m, 50% for 30m before full cutover.
- Rollback window: automatic rollback if error rate > 3% sustained for 10m during canary. Manual rollback otherwise.

5) Owners & next steps
- Karthik: validate TF variable aliases and ensure modules accept both old and new var names.
- Lauren: refine playbook for pre-drain compliance hook and provide contact for BlueHarbor SRE to test.
- Marissa: confirm pilot dates and coordinate the working session slot.

I’ll be on the Tue/Wed slots Ravi suggested. If BlueHarbor can send SIEM intake info that will unblock wiring.

Neha
Senior Manager, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: PrivDeploy IaC: Drain + Circuit-Breaker Matrix and Rollout Orchestration — next steps

All — quick summary and actions so we have a single source of truth: 

Decisions:
- Use CB defaults: 5% error over 5m to trip in pilot (per-tenant) with full auditable events to SIEM.
- Drain: default 120s, expose via Helm as values.global.drainGraceSec; include pre-drain Ansible hook for BlueHarbor compliance scatter.
- Module ownership: Terraform = networking & routing; Helm = service config; Ansible = host operations. TF modules will keep deprecated aliases for one release and include migration notes.

Action items and owners:
- BlueHarbor: provide SIEM intake endpoint + auth token (Ravi) — due Tue EOD PT.
- Karthik: finalize TF alias patch and open PR with migration notes — due Mon EOD PT.
- Lauren: publish playbook-draft.md to the shared Drive and schedule a 60m run-through with BlueHarbor SRE — due Wed 5/26.
- Neha: add CI gating jobs (traffic-sim + smoke) to staging pipeline and share the Jenkins/GitLab job ids — due Thu 5/27.
- Marissa: book working session Tue 10:30–11:30 PT (tentative) and confirm pilot target week June 14.

If we’re good on these, I’ll close this thread and convert attachments into the working doc for the session. Thanks everyone — looking forward to the pilot.

Marissa
SVP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
